note: Anti-NGF antibodies reached IC/BPS on chemical-cystitis rodent models; a small tanezumab POC was positive, the dose-ranging trial was stopped for futility, and ASP6294 later missed too.
label: IC/BPS (anti-NGF)

engagement.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
engagement.note: Bladder NGF drove hyper-reflexia in rats and sequestration blocked it; no IC trial reported an NGF or bladder-reflex readout of target engagement.
engagement.short: Rat bladder NGF; no patient PD
engagement.quote: Administration of exogenous nerve growth factor into the lumen of the urinary bladders of normal anaesthetized rats produced a rapid and marked bladder hyper-reflexia similar to that seen with experimental inflammation.
engagement.confidence_note: Patient trials read from abstracts and registry records; ASP6294's EU CTR results list no PD endpoint despite PD in the title.
engagement.reason: No engagement readout in IC trials
engagement.judgement: Evans 2011 found no change in micturition frequency or voided volume (the rat cystometry readouts' nearest human counterparts) but did see fewer urgency episodes; these are symptom endpoints, not a PD readout of NGF binding, so not scored as engagement.

dose.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
dose.note: trkA-IgG 1 mg/kg set no human exposure target; no source bridges the cystitis models to tanezumab's IC doses (200 µg/kg IV; 1–20 mg SC) or ASP6294's 320 mg SC.
dose.short: No model exposure target for IC
dose.quote: Treatment of animals with the fusion molecule at 1 mg/kg, immediately before inflammation of the bladder, largely, and very significantly, prevented the expected increases in reflex excitability of this organ.
dose.confidence_note: Absence of an exposure bridge is a negative search over abstracts, registry records and the 2012 AdCom briefing.
dose.judgement: Hu 2005 (REN1820 in CYP cystitis, doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000155170.15023.e5) also reports a fixed dose only; none of the cystitis models dosed a member drug, so no member exposure was stated to compare.

efficacy.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
efficacy.note: Irritant cystitis in rats: trkA-IgG prevented and partly reversed bladder hyper-reflexia; later CYP-cystitis work with REN1820 agreed.
efficacy.quote: Systemic treatment with the nerve growth factor-sequestering molecule, but not control molecules, partially and significantly reversed established inflammatory changes, by about 30-60%, depending on outcome measure.
efficacy.judgement: Model family chosen as the NGF-sequestration cystitis work the class rested on (Dmitrieva 1997; Hu 2005, doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000155170.15023.e5). None dosed tanezumab, fulranumab or ASP6294, hence product_in_model false.

efficacy.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
efficacy.note: A single tanezumab 200 µg/kg IV dose cut average daily IC pain 1.4 points more than placebo at week 6 (n=64), the primary endpoint.
efficacy.short: Tanezumab POC cut IC pain 1.4 points
efficacy.quote: At week 6 tanezumab produced a significant reduction from baseline in average daily pain score vs placebo (treatment difference [LS mean, 90% CI] was -1.4 [-2.2, -0.5]).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract only; NCT00601484 registry results (posted 2021-05-13) give LS mean difference -1.36, 90% CI -2.203 to -0.510.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by us: Evans does not set the rodent data beside the trial in its abstract. Direction only, as the rat readouts (reflex excitability) and the human endpoint (NRS pain) are not on one scale.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: sign of change in bladder pain / hyper-reflexia vs control

efficacy.model: Chemical cystitis in rats/mice with NGF sequestration
efficacy.note: Tanezumab's 205-patient dose-ranging IC trial (1–20 mg SC) was stopped for futility; ASP6294 320 mg SC later missed its primary pain endpoint too.
efficacy.short: Larger tanezumab IC trial stopped for futility
efficacy.quote: A second study in patients with interstitial cystitis was impacted by the clinical hold and terminated for futility.
efficacy.confidence_note: Sponsor briefing for the 2012 FDA Arthritis Advisory Committee; the per-arm numbers come from the later registry posting.
efficacy.judgement: Called contra over the earlier same because the class's adequately sized IC trials both missed and the futile one is the same drug as the POC. Year is 2012, the first public statement of futility; NCT00999518 results (posted 2021-08-03) show week-8 differences vs placebo of -0.03 to -0.23, all 95% CIs crossing zero, though the trial was cut short by the July 2010 hold. ASP6294 (NCT03282318) and the registry posting are listed in patient_trials because they change no status. Fulranumab's IC trial (NCT01060254, n=31) ended for the hold with no results. Nickel 2016 pooled analysis reports a benefit in women only, which I treat as post hoc.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: sign of change in bladder pain vs placebo

patient_trials.quote: This study was terminated on 16 November 2010 following a US FDA partial clinical hold for the tanezumab interstitial cystitis clinical study announced on 19 July 2010 for potential safety issues, and following a pre-planned interim analysis.
Analysis type superiority P-value = 0.591 Method MMRM Parameter type Least-Squares (LS) Mean Difference Point estimate -0.2

Women with interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome and patients with symptoms suggesting the concomitant presence of nonurological associated somatic syndromes were more likely to experience significant pain reduction with tanezumab than with placebo therapy.

safety.model: Primate, rat and mouse toxicology with bone and joint histology
safety.note: The IC POC saw headache and paresthesia, no joint signal; the toxicology package had not yet been compared with a patient outcome.
safety.short: Tox silent on joints; POC saw paresthesia
safety.quote: The most common adverse events were headache (tanezumab 20.6%, placebo 16.7%) and paresthesia (tanezumab 17.6%, placebo 3.3%).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract only. model_first_use_year 2008 is a proxy: the IC POC (NCT00601484) started 2008-03-17, and the tox package preceded it.
safety.judgement: The strip opens at the first IC safety readout, not at the proxy first-use year, because no source dates the toxicology studies.

safety.model: Primate, rat and mouse toxicology with bone and joint histology
safety.note: Three-species bone and joint histology at large multiples of clinical exposure found nothing, yet rapidly progressive OA in OA patients put the IC trials on hold.
safety.short: Joint harm missed; IC trials put on hold
safety.quote: The non-clinical investigations we have conducted found no evidence of an effect on the vasculature, bone, or joint in animals treated with large multiples of the clinical dose of tanezumab.
safety.confidence_note: Sponsor briefing document hosted by FDA (archived), not an FDA review; no IC trial logged an adjudicated joint event.
safety.reason: Joint harm not seen in 3-species tox
safety.judgement: The joint harm was seen in osteoarthritis patients, so the comparison is imported (imported_from MONDO:0005178); the briefing states FDA extended the hold to the IC studies on 16 July 2010. Rodents could have shown it: a later rat meniscal-tear model dosed with tanezumab reproduced the cartilage damage but not the bone response (LaBranche 2017, doi:10.1136/annrheumdis-2015-208913).
safety.model_filed: Tanezumab or murine MuMAb911 in primate, rat and mouse for up to 6 months; hip and stifle histology, micro-CT, bone biomarkers: no adverse bone or joint change.
safety.magnitude_basis: presence vs absence of joint destruction
